guide.title: Eclipse guide
guide.subtitle: Everything you need to know before {{eclipse}}.
guide.sourcesNote: Safety and exposure data verified against IGN, NASA/GSFC and the American Astronomical Society.
guide.readingTime: Read it before leaving home: mobile networks will be congested on eclipse day.

filterRequired.title: Certified solar filter required
filterRequired.text: Never remove your ISO 12312-2 filter to look at the Sun. The retina burns without pain and the damage is permanent.

totalityNow.title: Now you can look without a filter
totalityNow.text: You are within totality. Remove the filter and view the corona with the naked eye. Put it back on as soon as the first point of light appears.

totalitySoon.title: Keep the filter on until second contact
totalitySoon.text: You are still in the partial phase. Do not touch the filter until the Sun is completely covered and darkness falls suddenly.

annular.title: Annular eclipse: never remove the filter
annular.text: There is no safe moment during an annular eclipse. The ring of sunlight that remains visible can burn just like the full Sun. Keep the filter on at all times.

partial.title: Only a partial phase here
partial.text: The Sun is never fully covered at this location. A certified filter is required from beginning to end.

none.title: No visible eclipse
none.text: Even without an eclipse, looking directly at the Sun or through an unfiltered lens can damage your eyesight.

safety.cameraNote: Use your phone screen, not your eyes.
